thread_analysis.thread_summary: [COMPANY] (test lab/consultant) arranges a correlation test for [COMPANY], who wants to validate their own RF tester (a CMW270) against Allion's InterLab RF Test System ahead of Bluetooth Logo certification testing, using an Allion-owned reference sample/board rather than the customer's actual product. The thread clarifies the purpose and required reference-sample information for building a Test Plan, the three deliverables (test logs, a report, and an InterLab RF Test System description document) before lending the reference sample to the customer, and then walks through the physical cabling (SMA/uFL-SMA conversion cable) and tester configuration (Serial-over-USB, 115200bps, HCI DTM command selection) needed for the customer to connect the reference sample to their CMW270, including a USB-driver troubleshooting step if the sample does not respond.
all_questions_found: Can the Test Plan be created from the customer-provided QUESTIONNAIRES, or is a different reference sample's information needed since this effort is about validating Allion's own RF Test System rather than the Logo-certification target product?
What reference-sample information (applied voltage, test command type, RF tester interface, model number) is needed to create the Test Plan and QUESTIONNAIRES for the reference sample?
Is the intended approach to run the RF PHY test on Allion's own reference sample first, report results, and then lend that same sample to the customer?

Does the customer's choice to run a correlation test between their CMW270 tester and Allion's InterLab system (using the Allion reference board) mean a test sample from the customer is no longer needed?
Is the customer's question about cable connections explained by the reference sample having been sent without its SMA conversion cable attached?
Should the customer be asked to use whatever uFL-SMA cable they already have on hand to connect the reference board to the CMW270, before Allion sends a replacement cable?
What tester-side settings (interface mode, baud rate, DTM command type) are needed to connect the reference sample to the customer's CMW270 tester?
If the reference sample still does not respond after the recommended settings are applied, what should be checked next?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread distinguishes between the Logo-certification target product's own test items (covered by the customer's QUESTIONNAIRES) and a separate cross-validation exercise where the customer wants to confirm their own RF tester agrees with Allion's certified InterLab RF Test System, using an Allion-owned reference sample as the common test object. It also covers the physical/electrical setup needed to connect that reference sample to the customer's CMW270 tester: an SMA/uFL-SMA conversion cable bridging the reference board and the tester's measurement signal, Serial-over-USB operation at 115200bps, selecting the HCI DTM command type (as opposed to the alternative 2-Wire-style command type), and checking for a missing Windows USB driver on the CMW270 if the sample still does not respond.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: A tester-correlation exercise requires its own Test Plan and setup information distinct from the certification target product's QUESTIONNAIRES, since the object under test is a reference sample, not the customer's product; the deliverables for this exercise are the test logs, a report, and a description of the InterLab RF Test System itself, all handed over together with the physical reference sample. For the cabling/setup issue, the customer's connection question is best explained by a missing accessory (the SMA conversion cable) that Allion would have asked the customer to supply themselves had the roles been reversed, so the correct response is to first ask the customer to use whatever uFL-SMA cable they already have, and only send a replacement cable if they confirm they don't have one.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Treating the reference-sample correlation test as if it could be planned and executed using the Logo-certification product's QUESTIONNAIRES would miss the setup information actually needed (applied voltage, command type, tester interface, model number) for the reference sample. Assuming the customer needs a new cable shipped immediately, without first asking if they already have a compatible one on hand, risks unnecessary shipping delay and cost.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a customer wants to validate their own test equipment against the certification lab's system, treat it as its own exercise with its own Test Plan inputs and deliverables, separate from the certification target product's documentation, and don't assume a missing-accessory connection problem requires shipping a replacement before first asking whether the customer already has a substitute on hand.
